title: Optimized Protocol for Cytosolic DNA Extraction in Mammalian Cells
author: Jahun, Sorgeloos, et al.
materials: qPCR core kit SybrGreen no Rox

Here, DNA from the cytosolic fraction is extracted using spin columns. This section uses the QIAquick Nucleotide Removal Kit (Qiagen), and the protocol is adapted from the manufacturer’s manual.23.Transfer 4 mL of PNI buffer into 15 mL tubes.24.Transfer the cytosolic fractions into the tubes in step 23 above, and mix well by inverting the tubes several times.25.Transfer the samples into the columns provided, 650 μL at a time, each time discarding the flow through after centrifuging at maximum speed (>12,000 × g) for 30 s at room temperature.Note: Use of a vacuum manifold in place of a centrifuge for steps 25–28 saves a considerable amount of time.26.Add 500 μL PE buffer into each column and spin at maximum speed (>12,000 × g) for 30 s.27.Discard the flow through.28.Repeat steps 26–27.29.Replace the receiving tube with a new one and spin at maximum speed (>12,000 × g) for 1 min.30.Transfer the columns unto labeled 1.5 mL tubes.31.Add 100 μL of elution buffer into the columns.32.Keep at room temperature on the bench for 1–5 min.33.Spin at maximum speed (>12,000 × g) for 1 min.34.Discard the columns and keep the tubes containing the eluates on ice.Note: Concentrations of the DNA samples can be measured using a NanoDrop spectrophotometer or a Qubit fluorometer at this step.35.Samples can now be frozen at ‒20°C or used for the next steps.Pause point: Step 35 can be used as a pause point, if needed. Samples can be stored at ‒20°C until required for the next steps, but it is best to avoid multiple freeze-thaw cycles along the same experiment.

steps.title: Infect HEK293T cells with MNV
steps.instruction: Prepare and infect HEK293T cells at MOI 0.05 TCID₅₀ per cell, then culture for 18 h post‑infection.

substeps.instruction: Detach HEK293T cells with Accutase Cell Detachment solution (BioLegend, 423201) for 5 min at 37 °C.
Resuspend cells in complete DMEM (DMEM + 10 % FBS, L‑Glutamine, non‑essential amino acids, penicillin/streptomycin).
Count cells and adjust to 4 × 10⁶ cells · mL⁻¹ (aim for 2–3 × 10⁶ cells per replicate; 4 × 10⁶ per tube).
Centrifuge at 800 × g, 4 °C, 5 min; discard supernatant.
Resuspend pellet at 4 × 10⁶ cells · mL⁻¹.
Aliquot 1 mL (4 × 10⁶ cells) into each of six 1.5 mL tubes (three infected, three mock).
Add virus to the three infected tubes to achieve MOI 0.05 TCID₅₀ per cell (virus volume 50–300 µL so final volume is 1.05–1.3 mL); add the same volume of complete DMEM to mock tubes.
Incubate tubes on an end‑to‑end rotator at 37 °C, 10 RPM (10–20 RPM acceptable) for 1 h.
Centrifuge at 800 × g, 4 °C, 5 min; discard supernatant.
Resuspend cells in 1 mL fresh media; repeat centrifugation and resuspension once more.
Transfer cell suspensions to 10 cm dishes and add 9 mL pre‑warmed media per dish.
Incubate at 37 °C, 5 % CO₂ for 18 h post‑infection.

steps.title: Extract cytosolic DNA
steps.instruction: Isolate DNA from the cytosolic fraction using the QIAquick Nucleotide Removal Kit and spin‑column purification.

substeps.instruction: Transfer 4 mL PNI buffer into a 15 mL tube.
Add the cytosolic fractions to the PNI buffer; mix by inverting several times.
Load up to 650 µL of the mixture onto each QIAquick column; centrifuge >12,000 × g for 30 s at room temperature; discard flow‑through. (A vacuum manifold may be used as an alternative.)
Add 500 µL PE buffer to each column; centrifuge >12,000 × g for 30 s; discard flow‑through. Repeat this wash once (total two PE washes).
Replace the collection tube with a fresh tube; centrifuge >12,000 × g for 1 min to remove residual buffer.
Transfer columns to labeled 1.5 mL tubes.
Add 100 µL elution buffer to each column; let stand at room temperature for 1–5 min.
Centrifuge >12,000 × g for 1 min to elute DNA.
Discard columns; keep eluate tubes on ice.
Measure DNA concentration with a NanoDrop spectrophotometer or Qubit fluorometer (optional).
Store eluates at –20 °C or proceed immediately. Avoid multiple freeze‑thaw cycles (pause point).

steps.title: Extract whole‑cell DNA
steps.instruction: Purify DNA from whole‑cell lysates using the QIAamp DNA Mini Kit and spin‑column protocol.

substeps.instruction: Adjust whole‑cell lysate volume with PBS to a total of 200 µL.
Add 20 µL proteinase K; mix gently by pipetting up and down ten times.
Add 200 µL Buffer AL; vortex briefly and spin to collect liquid at the tube bottom.
Incubate at 56 °C for 10 min (heat block or water bath).
Add 200 µL 100 % ethanol; vortex briefly and spin to collect liquid.
Transfer mixture to a QIAamp column; centrifuge >12,000 × g for 30 s; discard flow‑through.
Add 500 µL AW1 buffer; centrifuge >12,000 × g for 30 s; discard flow‑through.
Add 500 µL AW2 buffer; centrifuge >12,000 × g for 30 s; discard flow‑through.
Replace the collection tube with a new tube; centrifuge >12,000 × g for 1 min to dry the column.
Transfer column to a new 1.5 mL tube; add 100 µL elution buffer.
Optional: let stand at room temperature for 1–5 min.
Centrifuge >12,000 × g for 1 min to elute DNA.
Discard column; keep eluate on ice.
Measure DNA concentration with a NanoDrop spectrophotometer or Qubit fluorometer (optional).
Store eluates at –20 °C or proceed immediately. Avoid multiple freeze‑thaw cycles (pause point).

steps.title: Calculate fold change (2ΔΔCt)
steps.instruction: Analyze qPCR data using the Livak (2ΔΔCt) method to obtain fold‑change of cytosolic DNA relative to mock.

substeps.instruction: Obtain Ct values from the qPCR instrument for each technical replicate.
Calculate the average Ct for each set of technical replicates.
Compute ΔCt = Ct_cytosolic – Ct_whole‑cell for each sample.
Determine the mean ΔCt of the mock‑infected samples.
Calculate ΔΔCt = ΔCt_sample – mean ΔCt_mock for each sample.
Calculate fold change = 2^ΔΔCt.
Record and plot the fold‑change results as desired.

description: In eukaryotic cells, host DNA is normally sequestered within the nucleus and mitochondria during interphase. However, leakage and accumulation in the cytosol can occur in conditions such as; (1) Infections with viruses, including Dengue, Chikungunya and noroviruses, where it is thought that lipid recruitment for replication complex formation causes damage to mitochondrial and/or nuclear membranes; (2) Cancer cells, especially those involving defects in DNA repair proteins; (3) DNA damage following exposure to radiation or chemicals such as etoposide; and (4) Cellular defect in certain proteins such as BANF1, TREX1 or DNase II. (For a recent review on leakage of DNA into the cytosol, see Miller et al.2). This protocol uses cell fractionation and column extraction to isolate DNA from the cytosol of cells, and relative quantitative PCR (qPCR) to quantify it relative to mock conditions. As an example, we use cells infected with the mouse norovirus (MNV), which was recently shown to trigger leakage of genomic and mitochondrial DNA into the cytosol.1 We used previously published primer pairs targeting 18S (nuclear-DNA1), GAPDH (nuclear-DNA2), the RNR2-TRNL1 junction (mtDNA1), the D-loop region (mtDNA2), COX2 (mtDNA3), and ATP6 (mtDNA4) genes.3 It is expected that users will have prior experience with qPCR. For an introduction to qPCR, see Nolan et al.4 While this protocol is based on extraction of cytosolic DNA from HEK293T cells infected with MNV, it has also been applied to RAW264.7 cells infected with MNV, as well as HEK293T cells transfected with the MNV NS4 protein.1 A similar protocol has also been used in EMCV- or Influenza A virus (IAV)-infected HEK293FT and MEF cells, and HEK293FT cells expressing EMCV 2B or IAV M2 proteins.5 Advantages of this protocol over others, such as those involving imaging, include; (1) It is quick (can be completed in as little as 5 hours, with only 3 hours of hands-on work); (2) It is easy to perform (does not require specialized skills
